items.stem: Define the term 'lean production'.
items.answer: An approach to operations that aims to minimise all forms of waste (time, materials, inventory, movement, defects) while maintaining quality.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, an approach to operations that aims to minimise all forms of waste (time, materials, inventory, movement, defects) while maintaining quality. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain how JIT reduces costs.
items.answer: Less inventory means lower storage, insurance and financing costs, less working capital tied up and less waste from obsolete or damaged stock.
items.markingKey: 1 mark lower holding costs; 1 mark working capital/waste. [2]

items.stem: Explain why lean production requires a flexible and multi-skilled workforce.
items.answer: Production responds quickly to orders and waste is removed continuously, so staff must switch tasks, work in teams and suggest improvements.
items.markingKey: 1 mark flexibility needed; 1 mark link to teams/kaizen. [2]

items.stem: Based in Lagos, Lagos Bites Ltd (private limited company) produces packaged snacks such as plantain chips and chin chin. The business has around 700 employees. Rising costs of imported packaging have cut its profit margins. Explain how introducing lean production could affect Lagos Bites.
items.answer: Points to develop for Lagos Bites: lean production minimises waste; lower inventory and unit costs; improved quality and faster response; requires reliable suppliers and trained staff.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: lean production minimises waste. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Lagos Bites: food processing, about 700 employees, private limited company in Nigeria; rising costs of imported packaging have cut its profit margins). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Lagos Bites, e.g. lower inventory and unit costs; improved quality and faster response; requires reliable suppliers and trained staff. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Venture capital investors expect it to become profitable within two years. Maple Learning Inc., a private limited company in Canada with about 260 employees, runs an online tutoring and test-preparation platform for school students. Explain how introducing lean production could affect Maple Learning.
items.answer: Points to develop for Maple Learning: lean production minimises waste; lower inventory and unit costs; improved quality and faster response; requires reliable suppliers and trained staff.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: lean production minimises waste. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Maple Learning: education technology, about 260 employees, private limited company in Canada; venture capital investors expect it to become profitable within two years). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Maple Learning, e.g. lower inventory and unit costs; improved quality and faster response; requires reliable suppliers and trained staff. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: The owners want to double the number of cafés within three years. Café Cordillera SAS, a private limited company in Colombia with about 900 employees, roasts coffee and runs a chain of 60 cafés. Explain the risks to Café Cordillera of using just-in-time inventory management.
items.answer: Points to develop for Café Cordillera: JIT holds little or no buffer inventory; supply disruption stops production; unable to meet sudden rises in demand; higher transport costs from frequent deliveries.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: JIT holds little or no buffer inventory. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Café Cordillera: food and drink retail, about 900 employees, private limited company in Colombia; the owners want to double the number of cafés within three years). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Café Cordillera, e.g. supply disruption stops production; unable to meet sudden rises in demand; higher transport costs from frequent deliveries. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Based in Doha, Pearl Logistics WLL (private limited company) provides freight forwarding, warehousing and lorry delivery services. The business has around 1,500 employees. Large customers are asking for real-time tracking of every delivery. Discuss whether lean production is suitable for all businesses such as Pearl Logistics.
items.answer: For: cuts waste and costs; improves quality; more responsive. Against: needs stable demand and reliable suppliers; cultural change; vulnerable to shocks. Judgement: the decision for Pearl Logistics depends mainly on its industry and supply chain, and also on its workforce skills.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Pearl Logistics: logistics, about 1,500 employees, private limited company in Qatar; large customers are asking for real-time tracking of every delivery). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. cuts waste and costs; improves quality; more responsive; arguments against, e.g. needs stable demand and reliable suppliers; cultural change; vulnerable to shocks. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on its industry and supply chain; its workforce skills; its competitive strategy. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Pearl Logistics, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: A major US retailer has asked it to cut delivery times from twelve weeks to six. Mekong Furniture JSC, a joint stock company in Vietnam with about 1,200 employees, makes wooden and rattan furniture for large retailers in the USA and Europe. Evaluate whether Mekong Furniture should adopt just-in-time inventory management.
items.answer: For: lower holding costs; less working capital tied up; less waste. Against: risk from supply disruption; loss of bulk discounts; demand may be unpredictable. Judgement: the decision for Mekong Furniture depends mainly on the reliability and location of its suppliers, and also on how predictable demand is.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [3]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [3]: uses case evidence (Mekong Furniture: furniture manufacturing, about 1,200 employees, joint stock company in Vietnam; a major US retailer has asked it to cut delivery times from twelve weeks to six). AO3 Analysis [5]: arguments for, e.g. lower holding costs; less working capital tied up; less waste; arguments against, e.g. risk from supply disruption; loss of bulk discounts; demand may be unpredictable. AO4 Evaluation [5]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the reliability and location of its suppliers; how predictable demand is; the cost of a stock-out. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Mekong Furniture, not a generic one. [16]

items.stem: Based in Seoul, Han River Games Co. (private limited company) develops mobile games that earn revenue from in-game purchases. The business has around 340 employees. One game earns 70% of its revenue and its popularity is starting to fall. Explain one advantage to Han River Games of reorganising production into cells.
items.answer: Team ownership raises motivation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. team ownership raises motivation; quality improves through responsibility; less movement and waiting time. 1 mark: explained in the context of Han River Games (video game development). [2]

items.stem: Explain two risks of using JIT for a business that imports components from abroad.
items.answer: Long supply chains increase the risk of delays (shipping, customs, strikes); exchange-rate and political disruption; no buffer stock to cope.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark risk, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: JIT holds little or no buffer inventory. items.stem: Its biggest customer, a convenience-store chain, wants deliveries twice a day. Siam Ready Meals Co. Ltd, a private limited company in Thailand with about 1,100 employees, produces chilled and frozen ready meals for supermarkets and convenience stores. (a) Define 'cell production'. (b) Explain one advantage to Siam Ready Meals of introducing just-in-time inventory management.
items.answer: (a) Organising production into self-contained teams (cells), each responsible for making a complete product or component. (b) Lower inventory holding costs.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark partial, 2 marks full definition [2] (b) 1 mark point (lower inventory holding costs; less working capital tied up; less waste of obsolete stock), 1 mark explanation, 1 mark application to Siam Ready Meals [3]

items.stem: Define the term 'critical path'.
items.answer: The sequence of activities in a network that determines the minimum duration of a project; any delay to a critical activity delays the whole project.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, the sequence of activities in a network that determines the minimum duration of a project; any delay to a critical activity delays the whole project. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain how critical path analysis can help a business manage working capital.
items.answer: Knowing the EST of each activity means materials can be ordered to arrive just in time, reducing inventory and cash tied up.
items.markingKey: 1 mark timing of resources; 1 mark lower inventory/cash. [2]

items.stem: Explain why identifying activities with float is useful to project managers.
items.answer: Resources (staff, machines) can be moved from non-critical activities to critical ones to prevent or recover delays without extending the project.
items.markingKey: 1 mark flexibility; 1 mark resource redeployment. [2]

items.stem: Based in Muscat, Muscat Dates & Co. LLC (family-owned limited company) processes, packs and exports dates and date syrup. The business has around 160 employees. Three family members disagree about whether to sell shares to an outside investor. Explain the consequences for Muscat Dates if a critical activity in its expansion project is delayed.
items.answer: Points to develop for Muscat Dates: critical activities have zero float; delay extends the whole project; extra costs and lost revenue; damage to customer relationships and reputation.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: critical activities have zero float. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Muscat Dates: food processing, about 160 employees, family-owned limited company in Oman; three family members disagree about whether to sell shares to an outside investor). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Muscat Dates, e.g. delay extends the whole project; extra costs and lost revenue; damage to customer relationships and reputation. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Lumen Robotics plc is a public limited company based in Singapore. It designs and builds robots used on factory assembly lines and employs about 2,400 people. Shareholders are pressing for higher dividends while engineers want more spending on research. Explain how critical path analysis could help Lumen Robotics complete a major project on time.
items.answer: Points to develop for Lumen Robotics: CPA identifies the critical path and float; focus management attention on critical activities; schedule resources and deliveries just in time; monitor progress and react to delays.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: CPA identifies the critical path and float. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Lumen Robotics: industrial engineering, about 2,400 employees, public limited company in Singapore; shareholders are pressing for higher dividends while engineers want more spending on research). items.stem: Battery supply problems from Asia have delayed several large orders. Tejo Mobility SA, a public limited company in Portugal with about 600 employees, assembles electric scooters and e-bikes for sale across the European Union. Discuss whether good project management is more important than good planning tools for Tejo Mobility.
items.answer: For: tools like CPA provide structure; identify risks early; communicate the plan. Against: tools rely on people to use them; leadership and motivation matter; unexpected events need judgement. Judgement: the decision for Tejo Mobility depends mainly on the experience of the project manager, and also on the size of the project.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [3]: relevant concepts/theory. items.stem: Tejo Mobility SA is a public limited company based in Lisbon, Portugal. It assembles electric scooters and e-bikes for sale across the European Union and employs about 600 people. items.answer: Estimates may be wrong.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant disadvantage, e.g. estimates may be wrong; time-consuming for complex projects; does not ensure quality or motivate staff. 1 mark: explained in the context of Tejo Mobility (vehicle manufacturing). [2]

items.stem: Explain two limitations of critical path analysis.
items.answer: Durations are estimates; it does not guarantee completion or quality; complex projects make networks hard to draw and keep up to date; it does not show costs directly.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark limitation, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Maple Learning Inc. is installing a new production line. The activities, durations and dependencies are: A (12 days, starts at once); B (12 days, starts at once); C (12 days, after A); D (4 days, after A and B); E (10 days, after C); F (10 days, after D); G (12 days, after E and F). Identify the critical path and the minimum project duration, and calculate the total float of activity F.
items.answer: Critical path A–C–E–G; duration 46 days; float of F = 8 days
items.markingKey: EST: A=0, B=0, C=12, D=12, E=24, F=16, G=34; LFT: A=12, B=20, C=24, D=24, E=34, F=34, G=46 [1]; critical path A–C–E–G (zero total float) [1]; duration 46 days [1]; total float F = LFT 34 − duration 10 − EST 16 = 8 days [1]. [4]

items.stem: Iberia Moda SA is a public limited company based in Madrid, Spain. It runs 180 fast-fashion clothing stores and an online shop and employs about 6,000 people. Online sales are growing quickly while sales in its high-street stores are falling. (a) Define 'earliest start time (EST)'. (b) Explain one advantage to Iberia Moda of using critical path analysis to manage its project.
items.answer: (a) The earliest time at which an activity can begin, once all the activities it depends on are complete. (b) Identifies minimum duration and critical activities.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark partial, 2 marks full definition [2] (b) 1 mark point (identifies minimum duration and critical activities; resources and deliveries can be scheduled; shows where float allows flexibility), 1 mark explanation, 1 mark application to Iberia Moda [3]

items.stem: Define the term 'enterprise resource planning (ERP)'.
items.answer: Integrated software that links all the main functions of a business (operations, inventory, purchasing, finance, HR, sales) in one database so information is shared in real time.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, integrated software that links all the main functions of a business (operations, inventory, purchasing, finance, HR, sales) in one database so information is shared in real time. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: What is the main benefit of an ERP system?
options: All departments share accurate, real-time information from one database
It is cheap and quick to install
It guarantees higher sales
It removes the need for any managers
items.answer: All departments share accurate, real-time information from one database
items.markingKey: All departments share accurate, real-time information from one database. Integration of data across functions improves coordination and decisions.

items.stem: Explain how ERP could reduce inventory costs.
items.answer: Sales, production and purchasing data are linked, so materials are ordered automatically when needed, avoiding excess inventory and stock-outs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark integrated real-time data; 1 mark lower/optimal inventory. [2]

items.stem: Lumen Robotics plc is a public limited company based in Singapore. It designs and builds robots used on factory assembly lines and employs about 2,400 people. Shareholders are pressing for higher dividends while engineers want more spending on research. Explain how an ERP system could improve the efficiency of Lumen Robotics.
items.answer: Points to develop for Lumen Robotics: ERP integrates data from all departments; better coordination of purchasing, production and sales; lower inventory and fewer stock-outs; faster, more accurate management information.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: ERP integrates data from all departments. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Lumen Robotics: industrial engineering, about 2,400 employees, public limited company in Singapore; shareholders are pressing for higher dividends while engineers want more spending on research). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Lumen Robotics, e.g. better coordination of purchasing, production and sales; lower inventory and fewer stock-outs; faster, more accurate management information. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

Three family members disagree about whether to sell shares to an outside investor. Discuss whether innovation in operations is essential for the long-term success of Muscat Dates.
items.answer: For: lower costs; higher quality; competitive advantage. Against: high cost and risk; marketing and HR may matter more; incremental improvement (kaizen) may be enough. Judgement: the decision for Muscat Dates depends mainly on the pace of technological change in its industry, and also on its finance.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. items.stem: Indus Sports Goods Ltd is considering an ERP system costing $800,000. It is expected to cut inventory holding costs by $150,000 a year and administration labour costs by $50,000 a year, with running costs of $30,000 a year. Calculate the net annual saving and the payback period.
items.answer: $170,000 a year; payback 4.71 years

items.stem: Define the term 'operational flexibility'.
items.answer: The ability of a business to vary the volume, range or delivery times of its output quickly in response to changes in demand.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, the ability of a business to vary the volume, range or delivery times of its output quickly in response to changes in demand. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why low capacity utilisation increases unit costs.
items.answer: Fixed costs are spread over fewer units, so fixed cost per unit and average cost rise.
items.markingKey: 1 mark fixed costs; 1 mark spread over fewer units. [2]

items.stem: Explain two ways a business could respond to excess capacity.
items.answer: Cut capacity (close a site, sell machinery, reduce staff) or increase demand (price cuts, promotion, new markets), or rent out capacity to other firms.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark method, 1 mark explanation). [4]

World cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months. Explain how greater operational flexibility could benefit Gold Coast Cocoa.
items.answer: Points to develop for Gold Coast Cocoa: flexibility means varying volume, range and delivery quickly; meet seasonal or sudden changes in demand for chocolate bars; offer customised products at competitive cost; reduce inventory and waste.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: flexibility means varying volume, range and delivery quickly. items.stem: Which best describes mass customisation?
options: Producing only for a single customer
Making one-off handmade products
Producing large volumes of products tailored to individual orders using flexible systems
Producing identical products in huge batches
items.answer: Producing large volumes of products tailored to individual orders using flexible systems
items.markingKey: Producing large volumes of products tailored to individual orders using flexible systems. Combines low unit costs of mass production with tailoring.

items.answer: High investment in technology.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant disadvantage, e.g. high investment in technology; need for multi-skilled staff; complex scheduling. 1 mark: explained in the context of Desert Bloom (hospitality). [2]

items.stem: Maple Learning Inc. has a maximum capacity of 25,000 units a month and currently produces 20,000 units. Monthly fixed costs are $150,000. Calculate capacity utilisation and fixed cost per unit. Calculate the fixed cost per unit if utilisation rose to 85%.
Which condition is essential for just-in-time production to work?
options: Reliable suppliers who can deliver frequently at short notice
Unpredictable demand
Large warehouses for inventory
Suppliers located on another continent with slow shipping
items.answer: Reliable suppliers who can deliver frequently at short notice
items.markingKey: Reliable suppliers who can deliver frequently at short notice. JIT depends on reliable, frequent deliveries.
